items.originalTitle: 利安·劳森感激回归红牛，但预计F1复出将“艰难”
items.summaryEn: Liam Lawson received a call from team principal Alan Permane upon returning to the UK, learning that Isack Hadjar had injured his wrist and that he would substitute at the Dutch GP. Lawson says he is grateful for the chance but expects his Red Bull return to be tough.
detailZh: 为什么“心怀感激”的利亚姆·劳森预计在红牛的F1回归将会“艰难”
在红牛因伊斯萨克·哈贾尔受伤而进行临时的最后时刻替补之前，劳森表示，自2025年仅参加两场大奖赛就被车队残酷解雇以来，他已经学到了很多。
度假后回到办公室的第一天往往会让人大受震撼。利亚姆·劳森周一抵达英国时就是这样，他原本以为要按照惯例为小红牛（小红牛）进行赛前模拟工作。
劳森打开手机后接到了领队阿兰·佩尔马内的电话，告诉他计划有变：伊斯萨克·哈贾尔手腕受伤，劳森将在本周末的荷兰大奖赛上替他出战。劳森的队友阿维德·林德布拉德在第二天才被告知这一消息，而角田裕毅则被从海滩上召回，接替劳森在小红牛的位置。
“于是，我的那一周很快就变了，”劳森在赞德沃特对包括Motorsport.com在内的媒体表示。
在这里的人员变动有一种微妙的循环感。正是在2023年的赞德沃特，在丹尼尔·里卡多在第二次练习赛中撞车并伤到手之后，劳森代表红牛的青训车队完成了他的F1正式比赛首秀。他抓住了机会，随后在2024年中期获得了与角田一起全职出赛的席位，接着在那个赛季末红牛车队决定不再留用塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯时，他又被提拔到红牛车队。
当时曾有人质疑，为什么劳森实际上插队到了角田前面，拿到了第二个红牛席位。而当劳森随后在出了名难驾驭的小红牛21上陷入挣扎，仅仅两站之后就被突然降级、由角田顶替时，这进一步证明了高层管理之间正在幕后上演的内斗所带来的破坏性。
自洛朗·梅基斯去年成为领队以来，为净化那个环境已经发生了许多变化，劳森本人也从在小红牛的18个月稳定期中受益，但接下来的日子仍将极具挑战。小红牛22并不是车队最出色的作品，冲刺赛周末的赛制使得车手们在进入排位赛之前几乎没有赛道练习时间，而且这可能是一代新F1赛车首次在真正湿滑的条件下同场竞技。
利亚姆·劳森在红牛的首次效力仅持续了两场比赛
“说实话，在红牛的一切都非常不同，”劳森说。
“对我来说，我知道我是来参加这个周末的比赛的，处于一个独特的处境，要尽力把握住这一个周末。这和开自己的车、待在自己的车队里完全不同。
“与此同时，自从（被红牛降级）以来，我也参加了很多场一级方程式的比赛，所以我学到了非常多的东西。我希望能够尽可能地把这些经验带到这个周末的比赛中来。
“但这肯定会很有意思。显然这是一条艰难的赛道，天气也会非常有趣——所以，是的，让我们拭目以待。”
这一周的时间线清楚地表明，劳森是这一角色的首选。他不仅在这场变动中没有任何选择余地，相关运作其实早已启动。而林德布拉德直到事后才被告知——这一点似乎让他感到不快，即便换作是他，也要面对更陡峭的学习曲线，因为他征战三级方程式和二级方程式的那几年，这两个级别都没有到过赞德沃特。
值得注意的是周四赞德沃特国际汽联新闻发布会上在场者的肢体语言。当林德布拉德被问到本周是否有过关于他升入红牛第二席位的讨论时，他一贯的爽朗消失了，把这个问题非常干脆地一脚踢进了长草区。
阿维德·林德布拉德承认，他的队友获得升入红牛的召唤是“更合乎逻辑的”。
“我不知道。我是周二才得到这个消息的，所以我不清楚，”他说。
当另一位采访者——也许有点不明智——再次回到这个话题时，林德布拉德的回答稍微多了一些。
“说实话，这是我第一次来赞德福特，”他说。“你知道，这是一个冲刺赛周末。我的新秀赛季才进行到一半，所以我认为，可以说，选择利亚姆是一个更合乎逻辑的决定。如果换成我，风险会稍微大一些。
“显然，作为一名车手，我本来是希望的。我本来希望得到这个机会。但与此同时，我完全理解他们为什么这么做。现在我非常专注于我自己的这个周末，努力做到最好。”
因此，我们可以推断，劳森被认为是所有潜在人选中风险最低的一个。角田裕毅直到本周末才驾驶过2026年的F1赛车，从一开始就不在哈贾尔席位的考虑范围内。据了解，在车队内部，劳森本赛季的身价有所上升，原因是他适应新一代动力单元那些往往晦涩难懂的驾驶要求时所展现出的速度。
当其他人（当然包括马克斯·维斯塔潘）几乎不停地抱怨这些新装备时，劳森却埋头苦干，充分利用现有条件。这一点，加上他在上赛季遭遇挫折后重建职业生涯时所展现出的韧性，使他成为显而易见的人选。他对前方任务的艰巨性没有任何幻想。
利亚姆·劳森三年前在阿尔法完成了他的F1首秀
“这是一个绝佳的机会，”他说，“显然，能被选中承担这样的任务，我非常感激。”
“但对我们车手来说，我们知道这绝对是件很难的事，要在一个周末之内去适应它。可以肯定，这会很有挑战性。
“说实话，我在一级方程式里经历过一些相当艰难的周末。就在整整三年前的赞德沃特，当时丹尼尔受伤了，我临时代替他上场。
“所以那绝对是迄今为止最艰难的周末，我也希望这次不会比那次更难。但这肯定会很棘手。
“显然，我也很感激过去能有那些经历，我认为正是它们帮助我成长为能够应对这样的局面。”
detailEn: Why 'grateful' Liam Lawson is expecting a 'tough' F1 return at Red Bull
Ahead of a last-minute substitution for the injured Isack Hadjar at Red Bull, Lawson says he’s learned a lot since his brutal axing from the team after just two GPs in 2025

The first day back at the office after a holiday can often be a shock to the system. And that’s how it was for Liam Lawson when he landed in the UK on Monday expecting the usual pre-race simulation routine for Racing Bulls.

After Lawson switched his phone on he received a call from team principal Alan Permane telling him there would be a change of plan: Isack Hadjar had injured his wrist, and Lawson would be standing in for him at the Dutch GP this weekend. Lawson’s team-mate Arvid Lindblad was brought up to speed the following day while Yuki Tsunoda was summoned from the beach to fill in for Lawson at Racing Bulls.
“So, then my week changed pretty quickly,” Lawson told media including Motorsport.com at Zandvoort.

There is a certain circularity to this changing-around of personnel at this location. It was here in Zandvoort, in 2023, that Lawson made his F1 racing debut with Red Bull’s junior team after Daniel Ricciardo crashed and injured his hand in second practice. He seized the moment and was duly given a full-time drive alongside Tsunoda mid-way through 2024, then promoted to Red Bull Racing when it elected to dispense with Sergio Perez’s services at the end of that season.

At the time, there were those who questioned why Lawson had in effect jumped Tsunoda in the queue for the second Red Bull seat. And when Lawson then struggled in the notoriously difficult RB21, only to be abruptly demoted in favour of Tsunoda after two rounds, it provided further evidence of the damaging civil war being fought behind the scenes between senior management.

Much has changed to detoxify that environment since Laurent Mekies became team principal last year, and Lawson himself has benefitted from 18 months of stability at Racing Bulls, but the days ahead are still going to be exceedingly challenging. The RB22 isn’t the team’s finest work, the format of a sprint weekend gives little track time before getting into qualifying, and this could be the first time the latest generation of F1 cars run together in properly wet conditions.
Liam Lawson's first Red Bull stint lasted just two races
“Everything's really different [at Red Bull], to be honest,” Lawson said.
“For me, I know I'm coming in for this weekend, and in a unique situation to try and maximise one weekend. It's very different to being in your own car, being in your own team.

“At the same time, I've had a lot of races since then [his demotion from Red Bull] in Formula 1 as well, so I've learned a huge amount. And I'd like to try and take as much of that into this weekend as I can.
“But it's for sure going to be interesting. Obviously it's a tough track, the weather's going to be very interesting as well – so, yeah, let's see.”

The timeline of the week makes it clear Lawson was the first choice for the role. Not only was he given no choice in the move, the wheels were already in motion for it to take place. And Lindblad wasn’t informed until afterwards – which appears to have rankled, even though he would have faced a steeper learning curve, given neither F3 nor F2 visited Zandvoort in the years he contested those categories.

It was interesting to note the body language in the FIA press conference on Thursday at Zandvoort. When Lindblad was asked if there had been any discussions about him taking the second Red Bull seat this weekend, his usual bonhomie departed and he gave the question a very sharp tap into the long grass.
Arvid Lindblad admits it was "more logical" for his team-mate to get the call up to Red Bull
“I don't know. I was given the news on Tuesday, so I don't know,” he said.
When another interlocutor returned – perhaps ill-advisedly – to the subject, Lindblad was slightly more loquacious.

“To be honest, it's my first time here to Zandvoort,” he said. “You know, it's a sprint weekend. I'm only halfway through my rookie year, so I think it was, let's say, a more logical decision to go with Liam. It would have been a bit more of a risk with me.

“Obviously, as a driver, I would have liked it. I would have liked the opportunity. But at the same time, I understand completely why they did what they did. And I'm very focused now on my own weekend and trying to do as best as I can.”

So, we can infer that Lawson was perceived as the least risky of the potential choices. Tsunoda, who hasn’t driven a 2026 F1 car until this weekend, was never in the picture for Hadjar’s seat. But it’s understood that, internally, Lawson’s stock has risen this season based on the speed with which he adapted to the often abstruse driving requirements of the new-generation power units.

While others (including, of course, Max Verstappen) have complained almost ceaselessly about the new hardware, Lawson has knuckled down to make the most of it. This, along with the resilience he has displayed in rebuilding his career after last season’s knockback, contributed to him being the obvious candidate. He has no illusions about the magnitude of the task ahead.
Liam Lawson made his F1 debut with AlphaTauri three years ago
“It's a great opportunity,” he said. “I'm very grateful to be chosen for something like this, obviously.
“But for us as drivers, we know that it's definitely a tough thing to come into and to try and adapt to in one weekend. For sure, it's going to be challenging.
“I've had some pretty tough weekends in Formula 1 to be fair. Literally three years ago was Zandvoort when, obviously, Daniel had his injury and I jumped in.
“So that's got to be number one toughest weekend ever, and I would hope that this is not tougher than that. But it's going to be tricky for sure.
“Obviously I'm grateful to have had those experiences in the past as well, I think they sort of help build you to something like this.”

items.titleZh: 维斯塔潘续约红牛后F1车手市场的下一步走向
items.summaryZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘与红牛续约至2030年底，这几乎排除了2026年F1前四强车队明年阵容的重大变动，但车手市场仍有一些悬而未决的问题待解决。
items.originalTitle: 维斯塔潘续约后，F1车手市场下一步何去何从
items.summaryEn: Max Verstappen's recommitment to Red Bull until the end of 2030 has all but ruled out major changes among F1 2026's top four teams next year, but several interesting driver market questions remain unresolved.
detailZh: 随着马克斯·维斯塔潘重新承诺留在红牛直至2030年底，F1车手市场的一大块拼图已经落定。
这几乎排除了明年F1 2026四大车队之间发生重大变动的可能性，但仍有一些耐人寻味的车手市场问题悬而未决。
既然维斯塔潘已决定不进行爆炸性的离开，以下是现在需要解决的主要遗留问题。
红牛的内部选择现在变得更加复杂
既然维斯塔潘（Verstappen）在‘27赛季的位置已经确定，红牛就可以把注意力转向其车队中另外三个席位。伊萨克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）有望留任，但他的伤病加上利亚姆·劳森（劳森）的替补出场，两者的结合可能会改变这一局面。
不过，小红牛的车手阵容更有可能发生变化。尼古拉·索洛夫（Nikola Tsolov）在二级方程式（Formula 2）中领跑积分榜的表现意味着他正接近被提拔，成为红牛的下一个候补人选，而这可能会带来一个问题。
红牛希望在阿维德·林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）强劲的新秀赛季之后将其留在F1，但劳森在另一辆小红牛赛车中的表现表明，他正在做车队需要他做的全部工作。
这意味着，在决定其B队2027年阵容时，红牛很可能必须决定：是想要加速索洛夫的成长，还是继续坚持今年一直表现出色的车手组合。——Edd Straw
阿隆索把自己面临的重大决定推迟了。
费尔南多·阿隆索曾一度看似是车手市场上关键人物之一。
如果他决定这将是自己参赛的最后一个赛季，那么即便阿斯顿·马丁正在经历艰难的2026赛季，2027年也可能会留下一个潜在的有趣席位。
不过，尽管阿隆索在夏休期之前曾公开表示会利用八月来决定自己是否继续参赛，但他度假归来后却把这个问题往后拖了拖。
他说，他脑子里仍需要理清一些事情——好胜心是否还在、是否足以支撑他继续下去——尽管他表示，毫无疑问他肯定会在某个地方继续参赛，无论是F1、达喀尔还是印第500。
但他还耐人寻味地暗示，新合同的推进将取决于车队老板Lawrence Stroll和车队领队Adrian Newey的想法——而他在假期期间一直没有机会见到他们。
要与其中任何一人交谈，只有在F1比赛现场或他下次造访银石工厂时才有机会。
“和Lawrence以及Adrian坐下来谈，如果车队需要我继续开车，我会考虑的，”他说。
“如果我能在另一个位置上更有价值，我会很高兴，我会考虑，而且我也会感到开心。”
一方面，阿隆索的言论暗示存在一些不确定性——无论是对他自己还是对车队来说，接下来会发生什么都还不明朗。
但现实情况更可能是，需要厘清的主要悬念其实是阿斯顿·马丁在2027年能有多强的竞争力。
如果下个赛季的开局和今年一样，你很容易想象阿隆索会认为自己可以不必再全身心投入、再去参加比赛。
但如果本田本周末的升级展现出此前在测功机和匈牙利拍摄日所预示的潜力，并且阿斯顿·马丁能够从其B规格底盘上释放出进一步的改进，那么预计推动这份协议达成的热情会更多一些。
等到阿隆索能够与老斯托尔好好面谈时——最有可能是在银石工厂——赞德沃特站应该已经尘埃落定，阿斯顿·马丁的潜力图景也会更加清晰。
此外，达成协议也没有太大的紧迫性，因为近几个月与这个席位联系在一起的其他潜在大牌车手——如维斯塔潘和塞恩斯——都已在别处确定了自己的未来。
最终，事态的走向指向阿隆索将再次续约。——Jon Noble
阿尔派车队的执行顾问弗拉维奥·布里亚托利几个月前曾半开玩笑地表示，在他弄清楚梅赛德斯将如何处理乔治·拉塞尔和安东内利之前，他不会对皮埃尔·加斯利2027年的队友人选做出决定。
一旦这家德国制造商内部出现爆炸性的矛盾，就有机会趁虚而入、抢下银箭车队的这两位车手——这样的机会实在太诱人，不容错过，尽管其可能性非常渺茫。
但现在这扇门基本上已经关上了，这意味着现任车手科拉平托越来越有可能获得合同续约，只要他继续保持目前的表现。
这位阿根廷车手去年在阿尔派的开局并不稳定，他难以达到外界寄予他的高期望，并在早期经历了不少挫折。
但2025年年底更强劲的表现，以及这股势头延续到了今年，都表明他正在做一切需要做的事情来保住自己的席位。
但基于阿尔派目前在车队的实力排序中所处的位置，以及当下理顺赛车和车队基础设施是首要任务，Colapinto的进步符合他保住席位所需要的水平。
Briatore最近告诉The 比赛，Colapinto“从去年到今年进步了100%”，但他希望看到这种进步继续下去。
所以，如果Colapinto能像现在这样继续下去，完全有理由相信那份合同最终会敲定。
不过，他可能还得再等一段时间才能让事情尘埃落定——因为Briatore最喜欢的就是让他的车手保持饥饿感。- JN
Sharks正在盯上Ocon的哈斯席位
奥康在哈斯的合同中拥有2026年的选择权，但一段时间以来，他一直在朝着出口的方向漂移，手上有多个潜在的备选选项。
不过，他仍然在考虑范围之内，尤其是在8月休赛前表现有所提升之后。
问题在于哈斯车队还有很多其他选择，车队正在耐心地决定谁应该成为奥利·比尔曼的队友，比尔曼拥有2027年的选择权。
双方已达成协议，如果哈斯愿意，可以从迈凯伦租借F2锦标赛领跑者莱昂纳多·福尔纳罗利，今年早些时候他在赫雷斯测试2025款哈斯赛车时给人留下了积极的印象。
目前F2领先者拉斐尔·卡马拉也将很快驾驶这款‘25赛车，他也在人选之中。与他有合约的法拉利正在推动卡马拉获得这个席位。
然而，需要注意的是，法拉利对这个席位并没有直接的控制权。
detailEn: A big piece of the Formula 1 driver market has fallen into place with Max Verstappen's recommitment to Red Bull until the end of 2030.
It's all but ruled out any major changes among F1 2026's top four teams for next year, but there are still some interesting lingering driver market questions.
Here are the major outstanding issues to resolve now that Verstappen's decided not to make a bombshell departure.
Red Bull’s in-house choice is now more complex

Now that Verstappen’s place is certain for ‘27, Red Bull can turn its attention to the other three seats in its stable. Isack Hadjar is on course to remain, but there is the possibility that the combination of his injury and Liam Lawson’s stand-in outing(s) could change that.

However, the Racing Bulls line-up is more likely to change. Nikola Tsolov’s championship-leading performances in Formula 2 mean he’s closing on promotion as Red Bull’s next cab off the rank, which could create a problem.
Red Bull will want to keep Arvid Lindblad in F1 after his strong rookie season, but Lawson’s performances in the other Racing Bulls car means he’s doing exactly the job the team needs him to.

This means that, when it comes to deciding on its B-team’s 2027 line-up, Red Bull will likely have to decide if it wants to accelerate the progress of Tsolov, or stick with a driver line-up that has served it well this year. - Edd Straw
Alonso has deferred his own big decision
Fernando Alonso had appeared at one point to be one of the key players in the driver market.
If he'd decided this was going to be his last season competing, then it could have left – even though Aston Martin is having a difficult 2026 season – a potentially interesting seat open for 2027.

But despite having spoken openly before the summer break of using August to make a call on whether or not he wanted to continue, Alonso has returned from his holidays kicking the can down the road a little bit.

He said he still needed things to be sorted in his own head about whether the competitive drive was still there for him to carry on – even though he says there is no doubt he will be competing somewhere, whether that is F1, Dakar or the Indy 500.

But he also intriguingly suggested that any movement on getting his fresh contract sorted would rest on what team owner Lawrence Stroll and team boss Adrian Newey wanted – and he had not had the chance to see them over the break.
An opportunity for a chat with either would only come at an F1 race or during his next visit to the Silverstone factory.
“Sitting with Lawrence and Adrian, if the need for the team is for me to drive, I will consider,” he said.
“I will be happy if I can be more valuable in another position, I will consider and I will be happy as well.”
On one hand Alonso’s comments suggest that there is some uncertainty – from both himself and the team about what goes on next.
But the reality is probably more that the main ambiguity that needs clearing up is how competitive Aston Martin can be in 2027.
If next season starts like this year did, you could easily see Alonso thinking that he could do without the commitment of going all in and racing again.

But if Honda’s upgrade this weekend shows the promise that has been teased from the dynos and the Hungary filming day, and Aston Martin can unleash further improvements from its B-spec chassis, then expect a tad more enthusiasm to get that deal over the line.
By the time Alonso gets to see Stroll Sr properly, most likely at the Silverstone factory, Zandvoort will be in the bag and the picture of Aston Martin’s potential will be clearer.

And there is also no huge rush to get a deal over the line as other potential big-name candidates – like Max Verstappen and Carlos Sainz – linked with the seat over recent months have all locked themselves down elsewhere.
In the end, the direction of travel points towards another contract extension for Alonso. - Jon Noble

Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore had cheekily suggested a few months ago that he would hold fire on making a call on who Pierre Gasly’s team-mate in 2027 would be until he knew what Mercedes was doing with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.
The opportunity to exploit any explosive fall out at the German manufacturer and grab on the Silver Arrows pair was too good a one to miss - even if it was very remote.
But with that door pretty much shut now, it means incumbent Franco Colapinto is increasingly likely to get a contract extension so long as he continues doing what he's doing right now.
The Argentine had a shaky start to life at Alpine last year, as he struggled to meet the high expectations placed on his shoulders and endured his fair share of frustrations early on.
But a stronger end to 2025, and with momentum having carried through into this year, has pointed to him doing everything he needs to stay.

But based on where Alpine is in the pecking order, and that sorting out its car and team infrastructure right now is the main priority, Colapinto’s progress is in line with what is needed for him to keep his seat.
Briatore told The Race recently that Colapinto was “from last year to this year, improving 100%,” but wanted to see that development continue.
So if Colapinto keeps going like now, there is every reason to believe that deal will get across the line.
He may just have to wait a little bit for things to be settled though - as Briatore likes nothing more than keeping his drivers hungry. - JN
Sharks are circling for Ocon's Haas seat
Esteban Ocon has an option in his Haas contract for 2026, but for some time he’s been drifting towards the exit door with multiple potential alternatives.
However, he’s still in the mix, especially after an improved performance before the August break.
The trouble is that there are many other options for Haas, which is taking a patient approach to deciding who should be team-mate to Ollie Bearman, who is under option for 2027.

An agreement exists to take Formula 2 championship leader Leonardo Fornaroli on loan from McLaren should Haas want to, and he made a positive impression when testing a 2025 Haas at Jerez earlier this year.
Current F2 frontrunner Rafael Camara will also drive the ‘25 car soon and is also in the mix. Ferrari, which has him under contract, is pushing for Camara to get the place.
However, it’s important to note that Ferrari has no direct control over the seat.

items.summaryEn: Formula 1 will race for the final time around the sand dunes of Zandvoort this weekend as the seaside circuit hosts its last Dutch Grand Prix, and Motorsport.com writers look back on their favourite memories there.
detailZh: 再见赞德沃特：我们的作者眼中F1荷兰大奖赛的精彩瞬间
随着赞德沃特本周末举办最后一届F1荷兰大奖赛，我们来回顾一下这座海滨赛道上属于我们个人的精彩时刻
比赛冠军马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
本周末，F1赛车将最后一次在赞德沃特的沙丘间飞驰，这座海滨赛道即将迎来它的最后一届荷兰大奖赛。在2021年重返赛历之后，这条赛道宣布将于2024年底退出。
在方格旗最后一次挥舞之前，我们的撰稿人回顾了他们在赞德沃特最珍贵的一些回忆——包括精彩的比赛、海滨的环境以及热情似火的橙色人群。
对我而言，2021年的那一届仍然是最难忘的赞德沃特经历。在这项赛车运动的巅峰赛事于1985年的比赛之后离开荷兰后，没有人认为重返荷兰沙丘地带是可能的。因此，看到一级方程式的马戏团再次降临赞德沃特赛道，几乎有种超现实的感觉。
除此之外，当时新冠疫情限制措施仍在实施，这使得荷兰大奖赛成为该国首批重大体育赛事之一——在此之前，赛事组织者几乎没有机会举办如此规模的活动。
最后同样重要的一点是：那是2021年，一级方程式历史上最激烈的车队年度总冠军争夺战之一的一年。
在八月的那个周日，所有这些要素齐聚一堂，尤其是在发车区上。国歌奏毕、车手们走回自己的赛车进入状态之后，你能感受到现场每个人身上都弥漫着紧张气氛。
什么最能概括这场为期四天的荷兰大奖赛盛会？当维斯塔潘戴上头盔的那一刻，DJ 决定再次通过音响高声播放《Super Max》——这大概是当天第五十次播放了。
再加上当时2021年的赛车被证明很难超车，这意味着一切都取决于起步，而整个橙色军团只为了一个人而来。维斯塔潘肩上的压力是巨大的。
令赛事推广方欣喜的是，这位荷兰车手最终顶住了所有这些压力，为这场赛事献上了一位梦想中的冠军。
当时任红牛车队领队的克里斯蒂安·霍纳在周日晚间离开赛道时，他恰如其分地总结了那个周末：“感觉就像我连续四天泡在夜店里没停过。”如今终点线已近在眼前，2021年那一届至今仍是最令人难忘的一届。

我还记得，当得知赞德福特将加入F1赛历时，我感到非常惊讶。虽然荷兰大奖赛的传闻已经流传了一段时间——随着维斯塔潘效应让荷兰人心潮澎湃，全国对F1重燃热情——但赞德福特自1985年底之后就离开了赛历，感觉实在太……怎么说呢，与这项锦标赛的愿景格格不入：锦标赛偏爱不惜重金打造的沙漠赛道，还要靠巨额公共投资基金去吮吸发展中国家的乳汁。多哈和吉达与一座小海滨小镇同时加入赛历，这种反差显而易见；这就好比博格诺里吉斯突然筹到了资金要办一场比赛……
但赞德福特承诺让自己的比赛与众不同，尽管可用场地十分紧凑。它对倾斜弯道的运用是一个聪明的解决方案，与3号弯和14号弯的形态截然不同。再加上车迷们把节日般的氛围带进了赛场，整个赛道被一层烟雾缭绕的橙色面纱所笼罩，充满个性与喧嚣。
2023年我和前同事马特·基尤报道那场比赛时，我们干了一件相当漂亮的事：在赞德福特本地找到了一间爱彼迎民宿。从公寓步行到赛道只需轻快的半小时，本来很方便，直到周六早上天空下起了倾盆大雨。那天剩下的时间我们都穿着微微潮湿的衣服，因为提供的雨伞几乎提供不了什么保护和喘息的机会……
正如我之前提到过的，去一条赛道工作，结束一天的工作后，步行五分钟就能到一家海边餐厅吃晚餐，这种感觉很有些不协调。不过这也让体验更加愉快；你会珍惜那些能提供一些与众不同体验的赛道，而赞德沃特无疑做到了这一点。
在赛道边看车同样令人难忘。看到车手们在倾斜的三号弯外线上试探、几乎贴到墙上，是一种全新的体验；再往下走一段，看他们通过五号弯和六号弯的曲折处时擦着地面驶过，更能体会到他们每一圈都得多么拼命；赛道上几乎没有可以让车手放松的地方，只有真正进入节奏，才能跑出成功的一圈。
比赛本身只能说一般——对于一条技术性强且狭窄的赛道来说，这大概在预料之中，尽管根据天气和具体情况，偶尔也会超出预期。那么，F1 的损失就是电动方程式（Formula E）的收获——我认为第四代（Gen4）赛车在这段海滨之旅中会有出色表现。
我最早关于观看电视转播大奖赛的记忆是1982赛季。那年发生的几起悲剧对于九岁的我来说并没有太多触动，但在赛季初的几场比赛中，我总是被两辆法拉利领跑的画面所吸引——看起来大多数时候都是如此——同时默里·沃克在解说席上兴奋地喋喋不休。
在东约克郡长大，意味着英国的大奖赛场地在地理位置上离我相当遥远。因此，当荷兰站的电视转播开始时——默里在直升机拍摄的赛道全景镜头中调动着观众的情绪——想到这个赞德福特既充满迷人的异国情调，又其实并不难抵达，实在令人着迷。
那个时代的夏日出游，自然少不了在布里德灵顿这类狂风肆虐的海滨度假地，或者在特别难得的场合去斯卡伯勒，被不由分说地按进冰冷的北海里。想到那片灰色地平线之外，竟藏着这样一个高级大奖赛胜地，真让人难以想象！

事实证明，这是迪迪埃·皮罗尼为法拉利赢得的最后一胜，不久后他便遭遇了终结职业生涯的事故。我对这场比赛的记忆是：他早早地驾驶法拉利驶入惯常的领跑位置，此后便无人能撼动。在 YouTube 上重看英国广播公司（BBC）的比赛转播，印证了这一印象。这正是1982赛季的缩影：雷诺赛车快却脆弱；涡轮增压赛车在单圈速度上占优，却常常在一团团烟雾中退出比赛；而总冠军的形势也和你记忆中的不太一样（此时是约翰·沃森领跑）。
年纪更大、眼光更挑剔的人会注意到那些细节：地面效应赛车像钟摆一样颠簸跳动，屏幕上的图形信息寥寥无几，解说员很可能根本不在赛道边，在没有场上争夺可描述的情况下不得不填满大量的转播时间。但在当时，它看起来确实非常激动人心。
接下来的那个星期四，当我在父母的店里读《赛车运动》杂志时，奈杰尔·罗巴克似乎表示了赞同。
“在最近世界锦标赛赛程中的某些地点之后，”他写道，“赞德福特看起来又像真正的大奖赛赛车了，让赛车和车手有机会舒展筋骨，摆脱二挡。而我们对这个地方的喜爱也许还因为，就在几周前，它似乎已经加入了斯帕、克莱蒙费朗和纽博格林的行列，被锁进了赛车历史的保险库。在赛季中期去那里，就像在超市货架上发现一瓶拉图葡萄酒。”
考虑到我父母是卫理公会教徒，奈杰尔要是想在他们的报刊店里寻找美酒，那可就要失望了。但在44年后的今天，赞德福特终于走进历史的长河，或许我们举杯畅饮一杯好酒来纪念它的离去，正是再合适不过的事。
骑车消遣、油炸食品和一级方程式
作为赛车运动网络编辑团队的一员，能去现场观看比赛周的机会少之又少，这意味着大多数情况下，如果我去现场看大奖赛，都是以购票车迷的身份前往。去年我就是以车迷的身份来到了赞德沃特。不过，因为我喜欢自找麻烦，我决定骑车去赛道……从伦敦出发。

在三天时间里，我和我那群“散兵游勇”般的伙伴骑行了近300公里，穿越了东伦敦的荒野、东英吉利平原以及（西）荷兰的平坦地带。一路上腿酸、爆胎，还遇到了几场倾盆大雨。但带着满满一包荷式华夫饼，又在我最爱的三明治店（鹿特丹的贝克与穆尔）补充了能量，我们一步步接近这座海滨赛道。在最后一段路上，我们汇入了数百名同样骑车前往的骑手，在找到的第一个自行车停车场匆匆锁好车后，我们赶在第三节自由练习开始时到达了赛道。
到了那里，我就被赛道的氛围深深吸引了。当然，在一片橙色的看台上，我们这群人中没有一件维斯塔潘的周边商品显得格外扎眼，但等到第五遍播放时，我们也扯着嗓子跟着大喊“哒哒哒哒”。那一年的赛道上的争夺也出奇地精彩，兰多·诺里斯就在我们正前方退赛，而伊萨克·哈贾尔则夺得了辉煌的生涯首个领奖台。
但到了周末结束时，最让我难忘的是车迷们的热情、看台上极具感染力的欢乐氛围，以及随手就能买到的薯条配蛋黄酱或油炸奶酪卷配面包。赞德沃特，我们会非常想念你。
狭窄而老旧的赞德沃特按理说不适合一级方程式，理由有很多，但它之所以能办成，是因为有三十万个理由。用前红牛车队领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳的话说，马克斯·维斯塔潘狂热的粉丝群把这个安静的海滨度假地变成了一个“夜店”。
自维斯塔潘年少时横空出世以来，这种支持就一直无与伦比，而赞德沃特的赛事组织者能够把这些车迷聚集到这座老式赛道里并让他们始终保持热情，这一点也值得称赞。
荷兰大奖赛在把一个大奖赛周末打造成一场持续整周的音乐节式盛会方面一直走在前列，尽管对于这么小的一条赛道来说，某些后勤安排仍然很困难，但赛事高度依赖火车和自行车来运送车迷进出赛场的做法，是赛历上其他推广方的典范案例。
那种火热的氛围让赞德沃特成为一站令人愉快的比赛，即使赛道上的比赛内容并不总能跟上这种氛围。
detailEn: Goodbye Zandvoort: Our writers' highlights from F1's Dutch Grand Prix
With Zandvoort hosting its final F1 Dutch Grand Prix this weekend, we look back on our personal highlights from the seaside circuit
Race winner Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing RB16B

For one final time, Formula 1 cars will race around the sand dunes of Zandvoort this weekend as the seaside circuit prepares to host its final Dutch Grand Prix. After its re-entry into the calendar in 2021, the track announced its exit at the end of 2024.
Ahead of the chequered flag flying for the final time, our writers look back on some of their fondest memories from Zandvoort - including the racing action, seaside setting and vibrant orange crowds.

For me, the 2021 edition remains the most memorable Zandvoort experience. Nobody had thought a return to the Dutch dunes would be possible after the pinnacle of motorsport left the Netherlands following the 1985 race. That made it almost surreal to see the F1 circus descend on Circuit Zandvoort once again.

On top of that, COVID restrictions were still in place at the time, making the Dutch Grand Prix one of the first major sporting events in the country after a period in which there had been very little scope for organisers to stage anything on such a scale.
And last but not least: it was 2021, the year of one of the most intense title fights in F1 history.

On that particular Sunday in August, all those ingredients came together, especially on the grid. After the national anthem had been played and the drivers walked back to their cars to get into the zone, you could feel the tension building among everyone present.

And what best summed up the four-day festival that is the Dutch GP? The moment Verstappen put on his helmet, the DJ decided to blast ‘Super Max’ through the speakers once again – probably for the 50th time that day.

Add to that the fact that overtaking had proved difficult with the 2021 cars, meaning everything hinged on the start, while the entire orange army had turned up for just one man. The pressure on Verstappen’s shoulders was immense.
To the delight of the promoters, the Dutchman managed to withstand all that pressure and give the event its dream winner.

When then-Red Bull team principal Christian Horner left the track on Sunday evening, he aptly summed up the weekend: “It’s like I’ve been in a nightclub non-stop for four days.” With the finish line now in sight, that 2021 edition remains by far the most memorable one.

I recall being very surprised by the news that Zandvoort was set to join the F1 calendar. Although a Dutch Grand Prix had been rumoured for some time, as the Verstappen effect set hearts in the Netherlands aflutter and the nation found renewed enthusiasm for F1, Zandvoort had been off the calendar since the end of 1985 and felt too... let's say, out of alignment with the championship's vision for no-expense-spared circuits in the desert and to suckle on the teat of developing nations with massive public investment funds. The juxtaposition of Doha and Jeddah joining the calendar at the same time as a small beach town was perceptible; it would be like if Bognor Regis suddenly found the funds to host a race...

But Zandvoort pledged to make its race different, despite the compact nature of the space available to it. Its use of banking was a smart solution and offered a very different profile to Turns 3 and 14. That, plus the festival-like nature carried into the circuit by the fans, offered personality and noise enshrouded by a smoky, orange-tinged veil.

When I covered the race with my former colleague Matt Kew in 2023, we hit upon a bit of a blinder as we found an Airbnb in Zandvoort itself. It took a brisk half-hour walk to get from the apartment to the circuit, convenient until the heavens opened on the Saturday morning. We spent the rest of the day in slightly damp clothes, as the provided umbrella offered little protection or respite...

As I've alluded to, it felt a bit incongruous to visit a race circuit, finish work for the day, and then walk five minutes to make our way to a beach restaurant for a spot of dinner. That made it all the more enjoyable, however; you value circuits that offer something a bit different, and Zandvoort certainly did so.

Watching the cars trackside was equally memorable. Seeing the drivers flirt with the outside line at the banked Turn 3 and get ever-so-close to the wall was a new experience, and meandering further down to see them scrape the floor through the kinks of Turns 5 and 6 demonstrated how hard they had to work with each lap; there wasn't really anywhere for them to relax, and a successful lap can only be achieved if a driver's truly in the rhythm.

The racing itself has been so-so - probably as you'd expect for a technical and tight circuit, although occasionally exceeding those expectations depending on the weather and the circumstance. F1's loss, then, is Formula E's gain - and I think the Gen4 machinery will excel on their seaside sojourn.

My earliest memories of watching televised grand prix racing are of the 1982 season. Its several tragedies were rather lost on the nine-year-old me, but throughout the early races I was captivated by the sight – more often than not, it seemed – of the two Ferraris leading while Murray Walker chirruped excitedly on the commentary.

Growing up in East Yorkshire meant the grand prix venues on UK soil were geographically rather far removed. So, as the TV coverage of the Dutch round got underway – Murray revving things up over an establishing helicopter shot of the circuit among the dunes – it was fascinating to conceive of this Zandvoort, at once entrancingly exotic and yet eminently reachable.

Summer days out in this era naturally entailed being dunked without ceremony into the bitter North Sea at wind-lashed resorts such as Bridlington or, on very special occasions, Scarborough. To think that this rarefied grand prix destination lay just over that grey horizon!

This was Didier Pironi’s last victory for Ferrari, as it turned out, before his career-ending accident, and my memory of the race is of him driving his Ferrari to its customary place in the lead early on and running unchallenged thereafter. Re-watching the BBC coverage of the race on YouTube confirmed that impression. It is the 1982 season in a microcosm: the Renaults fast but fragile; turbo-powered cars dominating in terms of laptime but often expiring in clouds of smoke; and the championship picture not quite how you recall it (John Watson leading at this point).

Older and more jaundiced eyes spot the details: ground-effect cars porpoising pendulously, little in the way of on-screen graphics, commentators who probably aren’t even trackside having to fill vast quantities of time in the absence of any on-track battles to describe. But it seemed very exciting at the time.
The following Thursday, as I read Autosport in my parents’ shop, Nigel Roebuck seemed to concur.

“After some of the places on the recent world championship schedule,” he wrote, “Zandvoort seemed like real grand prix racing again, an opportunity for cars and drivers to stretch their legs again, to get out of second gear. And perhaps our enjoyment of the place was enhanced by the fact that, until a few weeks ago, it appeared to have joined Spa, Clermont Ferrand and the Nurburgring, locked away in the vault of racing history. Going there, in the middle of the season, was like finding a bottle of Latour on a supermarket shelf.”

Given that my parents are Methodists, Nigel would have been out of luck scouting the shelves of their newsagency for fine wine. But as Zandvoort finally makes its way into the vault of history 44 years later, perhaps it’s only fitting that we should mark its passing by raising a glass of something nice.
Cycling for fun, fried food and Formula 1

As one of the desk team at Motorsport Network, the opportunities to get out to race weekends are few and far between, which means that, more often than not, if I do go to a grand prix it’s as a paying fan. And it was as a fan that I made it to Zandvoort last year. However, because I like making things hard for myself, I decided to cycle to the race... from London.

Over three days and almost 300km, me and my party of misfits traversed the wilds of East London, the plains of East Anglia and the flats of the (west) Netherlands. There were sore legs, punctures and a few monumental downpours. But armed with a bag full of stroopwafels and fuelled by a stop at my favourite sandwich shop (Baker & Moore in Rotterdam) we edged closer to the seaside circuit. On the final approach, we joined hundreds of other riders en route, and after hurriedly tying up at the first bike park we found, we made it to the track just as FP3 kicked off.

Once there, I was sucked in by the atmosphere at the track. Sure, the lack of Max Verstappen merchandise among my party stood out in our orange grandstand, but by the fifth play through, we too were bellowing “duh duh duh duh” at the top of our lungs. The on-track action was surprisingly good that year too, with Lando Norris conking out from the race right in front of us, and Isack Hadjar clinching a glorious maiden podium.

But by the end of the weekend, what stuck with me the most was the passion of the fans, the fun that was infectious in the stands and the easy access to friet met mayonaise or kaassouffle met broodje. Zandvoort, you will be sorely missed.

There are a lot of reasons why cramped and dated Zandvoort shouldn't work for F1, but 300,000 reasons why it did. Max Verstappen's ardent fanbase turned the sleepy beach resort into a "night club", in the words of former Red Bull man Christian Horner.

That support has been unparalleled since Verstappen first burst onto the scene as a teenager, but the manner in which the Zandvoort organisers were able to corral those fans into the old school circuit and keep them entertained deserves praise.

The Dutch Grand Prix has been a trendsetter in turning a grand prix weekend into a weekend-long festival, and while some of the logistics involved remain difficult for such a small circuit, the event's heavy reliance on trains and bicycles to get fans in and out of the circuit is a case study for other promoters on the calendar.
That electric atmosphere has made Zandvoort an enjoyable race to come to, even if the on-track product hasn't always been able to keep up.

detailZh: 再见赞德沃特：我们的撰稿人分享F1荷兰大奖赛的个人亮点
随着赞德沃特本周末举办最后一届F1荷兰大奖赛，我们的撰稿人分享他们在这条海滨赛道的难忘时刻
本周末， Formula 1 赛车将最后一次在赞德沃特的沙丘间飞驰，这条海滨赛道即将举办最后一届荷兰大奖赛。该赛道于2021年重返赛历，并在2024年底宣布退出。
在终点格旗最后一次挥舞之前，我们的撰稿人回顾了他们在赞德沃特最珍贵的记忆——包括精彩的比赛、海滨的环境以及充满活力的橙色车迷人群。
对我来说，2021年的那一届仍然是最难忘的赞德沃特体验。在1985年那场比赛之后，这项赛车运动的巅峰赛事离开了荷兰，当时没有人想到重返荷兰沙丘会是可能的。因此，当一级方程式的巡回大军再次降临赞德沃特赛道时，那感觉几乎是超现实的。
更重要的是，当时新冠疫情的限制措施仍然有效，使得荷兰大奖赛成为在该地区经历了几乎没有举办此类大型活动余地的时期之后，最早举办的重大体育赛事之一。
最后同样重要的是：那一年是2021年，一级方程式历史上最激烈的冠军争夺战之一的那一年。
在八月那个特别的星期日，所有这些因素汇聚在一起，尤其是在发车区。在奏响国歌、车手们走回自己的赛车进入状态之后，你能感受到在场的所有人之间逐渐升腾的紧张气氛。
那么，最能概括这场为期四天的荷兰大奖赛狂欢的瞬间是什么？当维斯塔潘戴上头盔的那一刻，DJ决定再次通过音响大放《Super Max》——这可能是当天第五十次播放了。
再加上2021年的赛车超车难度很大，这意味着一切都取决于起步，而整支橙色军团只为一个人而来。维斯塔潘肩上的压力是巨大的。
令赛事推广方欣慰的是，这位荷兰车手顶住了所有这些压力，为这场比赛送上了梦想中的冠军。
当时任红牛车队领队的克里斯蒂安·霍纳在周日晚上离开赛道时，他恰如其分地总结了这个周末：“就好像我在夜店里连着待了四天没停过。”如今终点线已在眼前，2021年的这届比赛仍然是迄今为止最令人难忘的一届。

我记得当赞德沃特即将加入F1赛历的消息传来时，我感到非常惊讶。虽然荷兰大奖赛的传闻已经有一段时间了，随着维斯塔潘效应让荷兰人心潮澎湃、整个国家重新燃起对F1的热情，但赞德沃特自1985年底之后就退出了赛历，而且它给人的感觉与锦标赛的愿景不太契合——这项运动当时追求的是不惜工本的沙漠赛道，以及靠巨额公共投资基金吸引发展中国家。多哈和吉达与一个小海滨小镇同时加入赛历，这种反差是显而易见的；这就好比博格诺里吉斯突然找到了举办比赛的资金……
但赞德沃特承诺让自己的比赛与众不同，尽管它可用的空间非常紧凑。它对倾斜弯道的运用是一个聪明的解决方案，让3号弯和14号弯呈现出截然不同的特征。再加上车迷们把节日般的氛围带进赛场，这里充满了个性与喧嚣，笼罩在一层烟雾弥漫、橙色调的面纱之中。
2023年当我与前同事马特·凯乌一起报道这场比赛时，我们想出了一个绝妙的主意——就在赞德沃特本地订了一间爱彼迎（Airbnb）民宿。从公寓到赛道只需轻快的半小时步行，本来非常方便，直到周六早上天降大雨。那天余下的时间里我们都穿着有点湿的衣服，因为提供的雨伞几乎起不到什么保护和遮挡作用……
正如我所暗示的，去一条赛道工作，结束一天的工作后，步行五分钟就能到一家海滨餐厅吃晚饭，这种感觉确实有些不协调。然而这也让一切更加愉快；你会珍视那些能提供一些不同体验的赛道，而赞德沃特无疑做到了这一点。
在赛道边观看赛车同样令人难忘。看着车手们在倾斜的3号弯试探外侧线路、几乎贴到墙边，是一种全新的体验；再往下走到5号和6号弯的连续曲折处，看他们擦着地面通过，更能体会到他们每跑一圈有多辛苦——基本上没有哪里可以让他们放松，只有车手真正进入节奏，才能跑出成功的一圈。
比赛本身只能算一般——对于一条技术性强且狭窄的赛道来说，大概也在意料之中，尽管根据天气和具体情况，偶尔也会超出预期。那么，F1的损失就是电动方程式（Formula E）的收获了——而且我认为第四代赛车（Gen4）在这条海滨赛道上会大放异彩。
我最早观看电视转播大奖赛的记忆来自1982赛季。那一年的几次悲剧对当时九岁的我来说几乎没有留下印象，但在赛季初的几场比赛中，我总是被两辆法拉利领跑的画面吸引——似乎大部分时间都是如此——而默里·沃克在解说席上兴奋地叽叽喳喳。
我在东约克郡长大，这意味着英国本土的大奖赛场地在地理上离我相当遥远。所以，当荷兰站的电视转播开始时——默里在镜头中直升机俯瞰沙丘环抱赛道画面中调动气氛——想象这条赞德沃特赛道，既充满迷人的异域风情，又似乎近在咫尺，实在令人着迷。
在那个年代，夏日外出自然会意味着在诸如布里德灵顿这类海风呼啸的海滨度假地，或是在非常特别的场合去斯卡伯勒，毫无仪式感地被按进冰冷的北海里。谁能想到，那片灰色地平线之外，就坐落着这样一处高雅别致的大奖赛举办地！

事实证明，这是迪迪耶·皮罗尼为法拉利赢得的最后一场胜利，此后不久他便遭遇了终结职业生涯的事故。我对这场比赛的记忆是，他早早地把法拉利开到了惯常的领跑位置，此后便无人能撼动。在YouTube上重新观看英国广播公司对这场比赛的转播，也印证了这一印象。这正是1982年赛季的一个缩影：雷诺赛车速度飞快却脆弱不堪；涡轮增压赛车在单圈速度上占据统治地位，却常常在滚滚浓烟中退赛；而总冠军的形势也和你记忆中的不大一样（此时领跑的是约翰·沃森）。
年纪更大、眼光更为挑剔的人会注意到那些细节：地面效应赛车像钟摆一样上下颠簸（海豚跳），屏幕上几乎没有什么图文信息，解说员很可能根本不在赛道现场，却要在没有任何赛道上的缠斗可供描述的情况下，硬着头皮填满大量的转播时间。但在当时，这一切似乎都令人兴奋不已。
接下来的那个星期四，当我在父母的店里翻阅《赛车运动》杂志时，奈杰尔·罗巴克似乎也持相同的看法。
“在最近世界锦标赛赛历上的一些地方之后，”他写道，“赞德沃特看起来又像是真正的（大奖赛）赛车了，让赛车和车手有机会舒展筋骨，摆脱二挡行驶。或许我们对这个地方的喜爱还因为一个事实而加深：就在几周前，它似乎已经和斯帕、克莱蒙费朗以及纽博格林一起，被锁进了赛车历史的保险库。在赛季中期去那里，就像在超市货架上发现了一瓶拉图酒。”
鉴于我的父母是卫理公会教徒，奈杰尔要是想在他们经营的报刊亭货架上寻找好酒，那可就要落空了。不过，既然赞德沃特在44年后终于走进历史的长河，也许我们举杯畅饮一杯美酒来纪念它的离去，正是最合适不过的。
骑行娱乐、油炸食品与一级方程式赛车
作为赛车运动网络编辑团队的一员，能外出参加比赛周末的机会寥寥无几，这意味着我大多数时候去看大奖赛都是以购票车迷的身份前往。去年我就是以车迷的身份去了赞德沃特。不过，因为我喜欢给自己找麻烦，我决定骑车去比赛……从伦敦出发。

在三天时间里、骑行近300公里，我和我那群杂牌队友穿越了东伦敦的荒野、东英吉利的大平原以及（西）荷兰的平坦地带。一路上腿酸、爆胎，还遭遇了几场倾盆大雨。但带着满满一包荷兰焦糖华夫饼（stroopwafel），并在我最喜欢的三明治店（鹿特丹的Baker & Moore）补充能量之后，我们逐渐靠近了那座海边赛道。在最后的接近路段，我们加入了数百名同样骑车前往的车迷队伍，在匆忙锁好自行车、找到第一个自行车停放点之后，我们赶在第三节自由练习赛开始前到达了赛道。
到了那里，我被赛道的氛围深深吸引了。当然，在一片橙色的看台里，我们这群人几乎没有马克斯·维斯塔潘的周边商品，显得格外扎眼，但等到那首歌播放到第五遍时，我们也扯着嗓子大喊“嘟、嘟、嘟、嘟”了。那一年的场上争夺也出人意料地精彩：兰多·诺里斯就在我们正前方退赛，而伊萨克·哈贾尔则捧得了辉煌的生涯首个领奖台。
但到了周末结束的时候，最让我难以忘怀的，是车迷们的热情、看台上那种有感染力的欢乐，以及随手就能买到配蛋黄酱的薯条或夹炸肉卷面包的便利。赞德沃特，我们会非常想念你。
狭窄又老旧的赞德沃特不适合举办F1比赛的理由有很多，但它能办成比赛的理由有三十万个。用前红牛车队成员克里斯蒂安·霍纳的话说，马克斯·维斯塔潘狂热的车迷群体把这个冷清的海滨度假地变成了“夜店”。
自维斯塔潘少年时期首次惊艳登场以来，这种支持便是无与伦比的，但赞德沃特的主办方能够将这些车迷引导进这条老式赛道并让他们乐在其中，这种做法值得称赞。
荷兰大奖赛一直是将大奖赛周末打造成贯穿整周末的嘉年华的潮流引领者，尽管对于如此狭小的赛道而言，其中一些后勤工作仍然困难重重，但赛事高度依赖火车和自行车来运送车迷进出赛场的做法，对赛历上的其他推广方来说是一个值得研究的范例。
那种热烈的氛围让赞德沃特成为一站令人愉快的比赛，即使赛道上的比赛内容并不总是能够与之相匹配。
detailEn: Farewell Zandvoort: Our writers' personal highlights from the F1 Dutch GP
With Zandvoort hosting its final F1 Dutch Grand Prix this weekend, our writers share their highlights from the seaside circuit

For one final time, Formula 1 cars will race around the sand dunes of Zandvoort this weekend as the seaside circuit prepares to host its final Dutch Grand Prix. After its re-entry into the calendar in 2021, the track announced its exit at the end of 2024.
Ahead of the chequered flag flying for the final time, our writers look back on some of their fondest memories from Zandvoort - including the racing action, seaside setting and vibrant orange crowds.

For me, the 2021 edition remains the most memorable Zandvoort experience. Nobody had thought a return to the Dutch dunes would be possible after the pinnacle of motorsport left the Netherlands following the 1985 race. That made it almost surreal to see the F1 circus descend on Circuit Zandvoort once again.

On top of that, COVID restrictions were still in place at the time, making the Dutch Grand Prix one of the first major sporting events in the country after a period in which there had been very little scope for organisers to stage anything on such a scale.
And last but not least: it was 2021, the year of one of the most intense title fights in F1 history.

On that particular Sunday in August, all those ingredients came together, especially on the grid. After the national anthem had been played and the drivers walked back to their cars to get into the zone, you could feel the tension building among everyone present.

And what best summed up the four-day festival that is the Dutch GP? The moment Verstappen put on his helmet, the DJ decided to blast ‘Super Max’ through the speakers once again – probably for the 50th time that day.

Add to that the fact that overtaking had proved difficult with the 2021 cars, meaning everything hinged on the start, while the entire orange army had turned up for just one man. The pressure on Verstappen’s shoulders was immense.
To the delight of the promoters, the Dutchman managed to withstand all that pressure and give the event its dream winner.

When then-Red Bull team principal Christian Horner left the track on Sunday evening, he aptly summed up the weekend: “It’s like I’ve been in a nightclub non-stop for four days.” With the finish line now in sight, that 2021 edition remains by far the most memorable one.

I recall being very surprised by the news that Zandvoort was set to join the F1 calendar. Although a Dutch Grand Prix had been rumoured for some time, as the Verstappen effect set hearts in the Netherlands aflutter and the nation found renewed enthusiasm for F1, Zandvoort had been off the calendar since the end of 1985 and felt too... let's say, out of alignment with the championship's vision for no-expense-spared circuits in the desert and to suckle on the teat of developing nations with massive public investment funds. The juxtaposition of Doha and Jeddah joining the calendar at the same time as a small beach town was perceptible; it would be like if Bognor Regis suddenly found the funds to host a race...

But Zandvoort pledged to make its race different, despite the compact nature of the space available to it. Its use of banking was a smart solution and offered a very different profile to Turns 3 and 14. That, plus the festival-like nature carried into the circuit by the fans, offered personality and noise enshrouded by a smoky, orange-tinged veil.

When I covered the race with my former colleague Matt Kew in 2023, we hit upon a bit of a blinder as we found an Airbnb in Zandvoort itself. It took a brisk half-hour walk to get from the apartment to the circuit, convenient until the heavens opened on the Saturday morning. We spent the rest of the day in slightly damp clothes, as the provided umbrella offered little protection or respite...

As I've alluded to, it felt a bit incongruous to visit a race circuit, finish work for the day, and then walk five minutes to make our way to a beach restaurant for a spot of dinner. That made it all the more enjoyable, however; you value circuits that offer something a bit different, and Zandvoort certainly did so.

Watching the cars trackside was equally memorable. Seeing the drivers flirt with the outside line at the banked Turn 3 and get ever-so-close to the wall was a new experience, and meandering further down to see them scrape the floor through the kinks of Turns 5 and 6 demonstrated how hard they had to work with each lap; there wasn't really anywhere for them to relax, and a successful lap can only be achieved if a driver's truly in the rhythm.

The racing itself has been so-so - probably as you'd expect for a technical and tight circuit, although occasionally exceeding those expectations depending on the weather and the circumstance. F1's loss, then, is Formula E's gain - and I think the Gen4 machinery will excel on their seaside sojourn.

My earliest memories of watching televised grand prix racing are of the 1982 season. Its several tragedies were rather lost on the nine-year-old me, but throughout the early races I was captivated by the sight – more often than not, it seemed – of the two Ferraris leading while Murray Walker chirruped excitedly on the commentary.

Growing up in East Yorkshire meant the grand prix venues on UK soil were geographically rather far removed. So, as the TV coverage of the Dutch round got underway – Murray revving things up over an establishing helicopter shot of the circuit among the dunes – it was fascinating to conceive of this Zandvoort, at once entrancingly exotic and yet eminently reachable.

Summer days out in this era naturally entailed being dunked without ceremony into the bitter North Sea at wind-lashed resorts such as Bridlington or, on very special occasions, Scarborough. To think that this rarefied grand prix destination lay just over that grey horizon!

This was Didier Pironi’s last victory for Ferrari, as it turned out, before his career-ending accident, and my memory of the race is of him driving his Ferrari to its customary place in the lead early on and running unchallenged thereafter. Re-watching the BBC coverage of the race on YouTube confirmed that impression. It is the 1982 season in a microcosm: the Renaults fast but fragile; turbo-powered cars dominating in terms of laptime but often expiring in clouds of smoke; and the championship picture not quite how you recall it (John Watson leading at this point).

Older and more jaundiced eyes spot the details: ground-effect cars porpoising pendulously, little in the way of on-screen graphics, commentators who probably aren’t even trackside having to fill vast quantities of time in the absence of any on-track battles to describe. But it seemed very exciting at the time.
The following Thursday, as I read Autosport in my parents’ shop, Nigel Roebuck seemed to concur.

“After some of the places on the recent world championship schedule,” he wrote, “Zandvoort seemed like real grand prix racing again, an opportunity for cars and drivers to stretch their legs again, to get out of second gear. And perhaps our enjoyment of the place was enhanced by the fact that, until a few weeks ago, it appeared to have joined Spa, Clermont Ferrand and the Nurburgring, locked away in the vault of racing history. Going there, in the middle of the season, was like finding a bottle of Latour on a supermarket shelf.”

Given that my parents are Methodists, Nigel would have been out of luck scouting the shelves of their newsagency for fine wine. But as Zandvoort finally makes its way into the vault of history 44 years later, perhaps it’s only fitting that we should mark its passing by raising a glass of something nice.
Cycling for fun, fried food and Formula 1

As one of the desk team at Motorsport Network, the opportunities to get out to race weekends are few and far between, which means that, more often than not, if I do go to a grand prix it’s as a paying fan. And it was as a fan that I made it to Zandvoort last year. However, because I like making things hard for myself, I decided to cycle to the race... from London.

Over three days and almost 300km, me and my party of misfits traversed the wilds of East London, the plains of East Anglia and the flats of the (west) Netherlands. There were sore legs, punctures and a few monumental downpours. But armed with a bag full of stroopwafels and fuelled by a stop at my favourite sandwich shop (Baker & Moore in Rotterdam) we edged closer to the seaside circuit. On the final approach, we joined hundreds of other riders en route, and after hurriedly tying up at the first bike park we found, we made it to the track just as FP3 kicked off.

Once there, I was sucked in by the atmosphere at the track. Sure, the lack of Max Verstappen merchandise among my party stood out in our orange grandstand, but by the fifth play through, we too were bellowing “duh duh duh duh” at the top of our lungs. The on-track action was surprisingly good that year too, with Lando Norris conking out from the race right in front of us, and Isack Hadjar clinching a glorious maiden podium.

But by the end of the weekend, what stuck with me the most was the passion of the fans, the fun that was infectious in the stands and the easy access to friet met mayonaise or kaassouffle met broodje. Zandvoort, you will be sorely missed.

There are a lot of reasons why cramped and dated Zandvoort shouldn't work for F1, but 300,000 reasons why it did. Max Verstappen's ardent fanbase turned the sleepy beach resort into a "night club", in the words of former Red Bull man Christian Horner.

That support has been unparalleled since Verstappen first burst onto the scene as a teenager, but the manner in which the Zandvoort organisers were able to corral those fans into the old school circuit and keep them entertained deserves praise.

The Dutch Grand Prix has been a trendsetter in turning a grand prix weekend into a weekend-long festival, and while some of the logistics involved remain difficult for such a small circuit, the event's heavy reliance on trains and bicycles to get fans in and out of the circuit is a case study for other promoters on the calendar.
That electric atmosphere has made Zandvoort an enjoyable race to come to, even if the on-track product hasn't always been able to keep up.

items.originalTitle: 角田裕毅赞德福特目标：享受比赛并拓宽2027年选择
items.summaryEn: Yuki Tsunoda will return to F1 this weekend at Zandvoort, taking the Racing Bulls seat after Isack Hadjar's wrist injury. He understands the circumstances will be challenging but wants to use the chance to prove himself.
detailZh: 角田裕毅的赞德沃特目标：享受乐趣并拓宽2027年的选择
面对重返F1的机会，这位日本车手希望充分利用它——首先要享受回到发车_发车区的感觉，其次要努力留下足够深刻的印象，以改善自己的未来前景
在伊萨克·哈贾尔手腕受伤后，角田裕毅获得了小红牛席位的机会，本周末将重返F1。虽然他明白情况会很有挑战性——赞德沃特是一场冲刺赛周末，而且他自去年年底以来就再没参加过比赛——但他仍然想利用这个机会证明自己。
自去年在红牛车队度过令人失望的一个赛季后，角田就失去了正式比赛席位。由于未能在马克斯·维斯塔潘身边交出成绩，他把车队的位置让给了哈贾尔，转而担任替补车手。
他目前在2027年重返正赛阵容（英文：发车区）全职车手席位的希望看起来很渺茫，因此正如Motorsport.com本周早些时候报道的那样，他一直在探索其他选择，包括印地车（英文：IndyCar），并且他已经与迈耶·尚克车队进行了谈判。
然而，这次意外的F1征召至少给了角田裕毅一个展示自己的机会——并有可能为他明年的选择拓宽道路。
“我是说，表现好总是件好事，这也是我的目标，”当被问及他在赞德沃特本周末的目标时，他告诉记者们。“不管怎样，我都必须拿出100%的表现。”
“而且说实话，有这样一个机会和没有这样一个机会，差别是很大的。因为你知道，显然在和车队交流时，总是要靠谈话来推销自己。但你始终希望通过驾驶来证明自己，所以这很好。”
角田裕毅坚称，他的个人优先事项永远是F1——不过尽管他明白自己的选择有限，他也愿意去其他锦标赛参赛，因为他不想再在观众席上荒废一年。
“关注那些事情不是我的工作，”他在谈到与车队的谈判时说。“我的意思是，我完全把（那些事）交给我的经纪人。我的工作就是开得快之类的事情。
“我的心态始终在F1。我的主要目标一直是驾驶F1赛车并取得一些成功。无论如何，这一点始终存在。
“不过，是的，我也不想两年都待在维修区里。我也想开车。所以，如果有某些事情可能发生，或者我找不到明年（在F1的）席位，我的意思是，我不得不去寻找其他系列赛。”
“但直到明年我踏上赛道的那一刻，我的心态始终都在F1。”
“在这里获得一个席位一直都是很困难的。我明白能够留在这里有多么不容易、多么特别。所以无论处于什么情况，我都非常感激。”
“如果这能成为明年真正在这里开车的契机，那我会非常高兴，也觉得自己很幸运。不过，这毕竟不在我能控制的范围内。所以我能做的就是享受比赛并拿出表现。”
不过，考虑到他对2026年F1赛车缺乏经验，角田裕毅对为本周末设定任何目标持谨慎态度。
“我认为只有一节自由练习赛会很棘手，”他说，“但正因如此，我没有设定任何期望。现在，我只是享受并找乐趣，这也是我很长一段时间以来想要的。”
detailEn: Yuki Tsunoda's Zandvoort goals: Have fun and widen 2027 options

Presented with an opportunity to return to F1, the Japanese driver wants to make full use of it - first by enjoying being back on the grid, and second by trying to make enough of an impression to improve his future prospects

Yuki Tsunoda is making a comeback to F1 this weekend after Isack Hadjar's wrist injury offered him an opportunity to take the Racing Bulls seat. While he understands the circumstances will be challenging - with Zandvoort being a sprint weekend on top of him not having raced since the end of last year - he still wants to use this chance to prove himself.

Tsunoda has been out of a race seat since last year's disappointing campaign with Red Bull Racing. Having been unable to deliver alongside Max Verstappen, he lost his place at the team to Hadjar and settled for a reserve driver role.

The prospects of him returning to the grid full-time in 2027 look slim at the moment and therefore, as Motorsport.com reported earlier this week, he has been exploring other options, including IndyCar, where he has held talks with Meyer Shank Racing.
Yet the unexpected F1 call-up at least gives Tsunoda a chance to impress - and potentially widen his options for next year.
“I mean, it's always good to perform, which I'm aiming for,” he told the media when asked about his goals for the weekend at Zandvoort. “Anyway, I've got to give my 100% performance.

“And I think, to be honest, having this and not having this kind of opportunity is a lot different. Because, you know, obviously chatting with teams, it's always [about trying to] sell myself with talking. But you want to always prove [by] driving, so it's good.”

Tsunoda insists his personal priority will always be Formula 1 - but while he understands his options are limited, he is open to racing in other championships as he doesn't want to spend another year on the sidelines.
“It's not my job to look at those stuff,” he said about negotiations with teams. “I mean, I completely leave [it] to my manager. And my job is to just drive fast and those stuff.
“My mentality is always in F1. My main goal is to always be driving F1 and have some success. That's always there, no matter what.

“But, yeah, I also don't want to be staying at the garage for two years. I want to drive as well. So, if there's something potentially happening or I couldn't find a seat for next year [in F1], I mean, I have to look for other series.
“But until the moment I hit the track next year, I'll be always in... My mentality is always in F1.
“It's always difficult place to have a seat here. It's not... I recognise how difficult and how special to be here. So, no matter what any situation, I'm very grateful.

“And if this becomes a trigger for next year, that hopefully I'm driving here, that's something that I'm very happy with and feel lucky. But, yeah, it's always... It's not in my control anyway. So, what I can do is just enjoy and perform.”
Still, given his lack of experience with the 2026 F1 cars, Tsunoda is cautious about setting any goals for the weekend.
“I think having one free practice is going to be tricky,” he said, “but that's why I'm not setting any expectations. For now, I just enjoy and have fun, which I wanted to have for a long time.”

items.originalTitle: 前F1车队领队：维斯塔潘尚未达到巅峰
items.summaryEn: Former F1 team principal Otmar Szafnauer believes that Max Verstappen, despite having already won four F1 championships, is still improving and has yet to reach his peak performance.
detailZh: 前F1车队领队表示，马克斯·维斯塔潘尚未达到自己的巅峰
奥特马尔·萨夫瑙尔认为，马克斯·维斯塔潘仍在进步，尽管已经赢得四次F1总冠军，但还没有达到巅峰
前一级方程式车队领队奥特马尔·萨夫瑙尔认为，马克斯·维斯塔潘仍在不断进步，尚未达到自己的巅峰状态。
在与主持人杰克·汉弗莱以及前法拉利比赛工程师罗布·斯梅德利共同参加的一期《高性能赛车》播客节目中，萨夫瑙尔谈到了他在围场职业生涯中所遇到过的杰出车手。
当汉弗莱请嘉宾小组说出他们曾共事过和交手过的最伟大车手时，扎夫瑙尔点名四届冠军塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔作为他共事过的最佳车手，随后又将话题转向他在指挥墙（指挥比赛的围栏）边所面对过的最强对手。
"共事过的最伟大车手是维特尔。交手过的最伟大对手，很难在迈克尔（舒马赫）和刘易斯（汉密尔顿）之间选择。"扎夫瑙尔解释道。
当被问及为什么不认为四届冠军维斯塔潘是最伟大的车手时，他补充道："嗯，我认为马克斯还没有达到他的巅峰。我觉得他还会变得更强。"
维斯塔潘目前在车手积分榜上以109分排名第六，落后积分榜领跑者基米·安东内利110分。尽管有传闻将维斯塔潘与退役或转会梅赛德斯或迈凯伦联系在一起，这位荷兰车手已确认他将继续效力红牛。
这位28岁的车手签署了一份续约合同，将让他留在米尔顿凯恩斯车队直到2030年底。维斯塔潘在合同公布后的问答环节中解释说，他希望继续与车队一起赢得比赛和冠军。
"这里就像我的第二个家庭，"维斯塔潘解释道。"当然，我来到这支车队时就是希望能赢比赛，而我们已经一起赢得了四个冠军。
"此外，当然是再次朝着这个目标努力。这是一件非常令人兴奋的事情。这就是为什么我在这里感到像在家一样。
"我对续约感到非常高兴。我希望车队也同样高兴。我非常开心。希望我们能继续一起努力，争取重回巅峰。"
detailEn: Max Verstappen is yet to reach his peak, says former F1 team boss
Otmar Szafnauer believes Max Verstappen is still improving and has yet to reach his peak despite already winning four F1 championships
Former Formula 1 team principal Otmar Szafnauer believes Max Verstappen is continuing to improve and has still not reached his peak performance.

During an episode of the High Performance Racing podcast alongside host Jake Humphrey and former Ferrari race engineer Rob Smedley, Szafnauer discussed the standout drivers he has encountered during his career in the paddock.

When Humphrey prompted the panel to name the greatest drivers they had worked alongside and competed against, Szafnauer named four-time champion Sebastian Vettel as the best driver he had worked with before turning his attention to the fiercest rivals he had faced while on the pitwall.
"Greatest I worked with, Vettel. Greatest I went up against, tough either Michael [Schumacher] or Lewis [Hamilton]," Szafnauer explained.
When asked why he didn't consider four-time champion Verstappen, he added: "Well, I don't think Max is at his peak yet. I think he's going to get better."

Verstappen currently sits sixth in the drivers' standings with 109 points, 110 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli. While rumours have linked Verstappen to retirement or a move to either Mercedes or McLaren, the Dutchman has confirmed his commitment to Red Bull.

The 28-year-old driver signed a contract extension that will keep him with the Milton Keynes outfit until the end of 2030. Verstappen explained in a Q&A session following the contract announcement that he hopes to continue winning races and championships with the team.
"It's like a second family for me," Verstappen explained. "And of course, I came into this team hoping for, you know, being able to win races and that we have won four titles together.
"Plus, of course, working again towards that goal. It's something that is very exciting. That's why I feel at home here.
"I'm just very happy with the extension. I hope the team is as well. I'm very happy. Hopefully, we can just keep working together and try to get back to the top."
keyPointsZh: 萨夫瑙尔是在《高性能赛车》播客节目中发表上述看法的，该节目主持人为杰克·汉弗莱，嘉宾还有前法拉利比赛工程师罗布·斯梅德利。
萨夫瑙尔在节目中讨论了其围场生涯中遇到过的杰出车手。

detailZh: Karun Chandhok 对 维斯塔潘 红牛合同的长度感到“惊讶”。
Karun Chandhok 表示，维斯塔潘 与红牛签下的新合同延续至 2030 年，这体现了他对车队长期动力单元的信心。
前 F1 车手兼天空体育分析员 Karun Chandhok 认为，维斯塔潘 决定与红牛续约至 2030 年底，表明他相信车队自主研发动力单元项目的长期潜力。
Verstappen 目前在车手积分榜上排名第六，红牛本赛季的赛车常常只是第四快的。尽管统治力下降，并传出退役或转投梅赛德斯或迈凯伦的传闻，这位四届冠军仍将自己的长期未来托付给了红牛。
Chandhok承认，他对这一公告并不感到震惊，但对合同的长度感到惊讶。
"我对合同的长度有点惊讶。我不惊讶他选择效忠于车队，"他向天空体育解释道。"我原以为合同会签到2028年底。他签了四年，这说明他相信这个项目的长期可行性。"
"今年，在许多场比赛中他们可能拥有第四快的赛车。他在车手积分榜上排名第六。这不是Max想要的位置，但显然他们已经让他相信，长期潜力比今年的表现更好。"
他补充道："只要看看最近两场大奖赛，他已经两次登上领奖台。车队立刻有了势头。这正是让Max留下来所必需的条件。他想看到进步。"
"考虑到红牛一路走来的历程，他们能自己制造引擎实在是一件了不起的事。
"他希望看到动力单元方面的进步。他希望看到车队的进步，而我觉得从他们本赛季开始时的状态到现在的状态——如果你看看这条轨迹，这大概就是他所看重的。"
维斯塔潘续约的消息是在威廉姆斯确认与卡洛斯·塞恩斯和亚历克斯·阿尔本续约之后不久宣布的。因此，目前F1车手中已有超过一半锁定了2027赛季的席位。
"我们总是喜欢F1里的好故事，喜欢一点意外，而且有一段时间看起来这个'转会季'会很精彩，马克斯会成为那个挑起风波的人。"钱多克补充道。
"有关他转会迈凯伦的传闻，把Piastri踢出去，然后又有传闻说他去梅赛德斯，因为Russell或Antonelli在那里看起来位置不稳。这本来会成为一个巨大的新闻，但结果证明这终究算不上什么'愚蠢赛季'。只能重新另想办法了。"
detailEn: Karun Chandhok "surprised" by length of Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract
Max Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract through 2030 shows his confidence in the team’s long-term power unit, says Karun Chandhok.

Max Verstappen's decision to sign a contract extension with Red Bull until the end of 2030 shows he believes in the long-term potential of the team's in-house power unit programme, according to former Formula 1 driver and Sky Sports analyst Karun Chandhok.

Verstappen currently sits sixth in the drivers' championship, with Red Bull often fielding the fourth-fastest car this season. Despite the drop in dominance and rumours of retirement or moves to Mercedes or McLaren, the four-time champion has committed his long-term future to Red Bull.
Chandhok admitted he was not shocked by the announcement, but he was surprised by the length of the contract.

"I am a little bit surprised at the length. I am not surprised he is committed to them," he explained to Sky Sports. "I thought it would be until the end of 2028. The fact he has gone for four shows he believes in the long-term feasibility of the project.

"This year, they have had probably the fourth-fastest car at a lot of races. He sits sixth in the drivers' championship. That is not where Max wants to be but clearly they have convinced him that the long-term potential is better than this year."

He added: "Just look at the last two grands prix, he has had two podiums. Straight away the team has momentum. That is what it was always going to take for Max to stay where he is. He wanted to see improvements.
"Making their own engine at Red Bull is incredible stuff when you think where they have come from.

"He wanted to see improvement on the power unit side of things. He wanted to see improvements from the team, and I feel like from where they started the season to where they are now - if you look at that trajectory, that is probably what he is buying into."

Verstappen's renewal was announced shortly after Williams confirmed contract extensions for Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon. Consequently, more than half of the current F1 grid is now locked in for the 2027 season.
"We always like a good story in F1, a bit of upset, and it looked at some point it was going to be a great 'silly season' and Max was going to be the instigator of that," Chandhok added.

"Talks of him to McLaren, kicking Piastri out, then maybe talks of Mercedes with either Russell or Antonelli looking vulnerable there. It would have created a massive story, but it turns out it is not so much of a 'silly season' after all. Back to the drawing board."
keyPointsZh: 尽管统治力下滑，并有退役或转投梅赛德斯、迈凯伦的传闻，这位四届冠军仍将长期未来托付给红牛。
keyPointsEn: Despite reduced dominance and rumours of retirement or moves to Mercedes or McLaren, the four-time champion has committed his long-term future to Red Bull.

一级方程式在本周末从夏休期回归赞德沃特，荷兰大奖赛将开启2026赛季的最后阶段，此前兰多·诺里斯在匈牙利取得了突破性的胜利。
诺里斯在夏休期前夺得了他本赛季的首场胜利，而基米·安东内利仍然领跑车手总冠军，梅赛德斯、法拉利和迈凯轮继续互有攻守。赞德沃特现在立即给所有车队提供了一个完全不同类型赛道的考验，而冲刺赛周末几乎没有时间让车手们慢慢适应。
荷兰大奖赛在今年还具有额外的特殊意义，因为赞德福特即将迎来现代时代的最后一场一级方程式比赛。马克斯·维斯塔潘将在这里参加他最后一场主场大奖赛，而红牛车队仍努力在赛季下半程寻找更多性能。
赞德福特是一条狭窄、快速且要求极高的海滨赛道，拥有倾斜弯道，容错空间很小。这个周末还将采用冲刺赛赛制，这意味着车队在冲刺排位赛确定周六冲刺赛发车顺序之前，只有一节自由练习。

Formula 1 returns from its summer break at Zandvoort this weekend, with the Dutch GP starting the final stretch of the 2026 season after Lando Norris’ breakthrough win in Hungary.

Norris took his first victory of the campaign before the shutdown, while Kimi Antonelli still leads the championship as Mercedes, Ferrari and McLaren continue to trade momentum. Zandvoort now gives the field an immediate test on a very different type of circuit, with a sprint weekend leaving little time to settle in.

The Dutch GP also carries extra significance this year, as Zandvoort prepares to host its final Formula 1 race of the modern era. Max Verstappen arrives for his final home grand prix with Red Bull still trying to find more performance in the second half of the season.

Zandvoort is a narrow, fast and demanding seaside circuit, with banked corners and limited room for error. This weekend also follows the sprint format, meaning teams have only one practice session before sprint qualifying sets the grid for Saturday’s sprint race.
Friday brings free practice 1 followed by sprint qualifying later in the afternoon. Here is everything you need to know ahead of Friday’s running at the Dutch GP.

detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔分享了他向女友卡门·蒙特罗·蒙特求婚的夏日假期细节
乔治·拉塞尔公开了他与长期女友卡门·蒙特罗·蒙特订婚的消息
梅赛德斯一级方程式车手乔治·拉塞尔公开了他与长期女友卡门·蒙特罗·蒙特订婚的消息。
这位英国车手在夏日假期期间宣布订婚，并分享了在海边烛光晚餐上这一特别时刻的照片。
在荷兰大奖赛前的车手新闻发布会上，Russell在分享求婚准备过程的见解之前，受到了大家热烈的祝贺。
"那一刻非常特别，而且那真的是一个非常非常好的时机。我为此花了很多心思，设计戒指等等整个过程都非常有意思，" Russell解释道。
"当我到了那个时刻，我其实说不出话来。当我单膝跪地的时候，突然变得非常紧张，但那真的很美好，所以谢谢大家。"
Russell补充说，在重返必将激烈的车队冠军争夺战之前，他得以完全从F1中抽离放松。赛季上半程过后，这位28岁的车手在车手积分榜上排名第三，落后队友兼积分榜领跑者安东内利 59分，落后排名第二的汉密尔顿 9分。
"是的，说实话，完全可以," 当被问到是否能够放松休息时他说道。"尤其是现在进入赛季下半程，对我们所有人来说都会非常紧张，所以就是要充分利用这两周时间，显然在假期的头10天我心里一直惦记着这件事，那真的很棒。"
这位梅赛德斯车手开玩笑说，他希望订婚能为他在赛道上带来零点几秒的优势。
"我希望它能带来零点几秒的优势。如果订婚真能带来零点几秒的优势，就连兰多[诺里斯]也会去订婚的," 他笑着说道。
"个人生活非常重要。我认为对我们所有人来说，我们的生活是如此忙碌。与我们共同生活的人是其中非常关键的一部分，他们会和你一起经历这些情绪起伏。显然我和Carmen在一起已经很长时间了。
“我认为这不会带来太大的改变，因为这么长时间以来，她一直是我生命中如此重要的人。所以，这只是更多关于完成我们需要迈出的下一步而已。”
detailEn: George Russell shares details of summer break proposal to partner Carmen Montero Mundt
George Russell has opened up about his engagement to long-term partner Carmen Montero Mundt
Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has opened up about his engagement to his long-term partner Carmen Montero Mundt.
The Briton announced his engagement during the summer break alongside photos of the special moment at a candlelit, beachfront dinner.
Appearing in the drivers' press conference ahead of the Dutch Grand Prix, Russell was warmly congratulated before he shared some insight into the preparation that went into the proposal.

"It was very special, and it was a really, really nice time to do it. A lot of thought went into it, and it was a really interesting process, designing the ring and doing all of that," Russell explained.
"When I came to the moment, I couldn't actually get my words out. It was like suddenly I got really nervous when I was on one knee, but that was great, so thank you."

Russell added that he was able to fully switch off from F1 before heading back into what will surely be an intense title fight for him. After the first half of the season, the 28-year-old sits third in the drivers' standings, 59 points behind his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli and nine points behind second-placed Lewis Hamilton.

"Yeah, fully, to be honest," he said when asked if he was able to switch off. "Especially coming into the second half of the season now, it's going to be very intense for us all, so just really making the most of those two weeks and obviously I had that on my mind for the first 10 days of the break, so that was great."
The Mercedes driver joked that he hopes the engagement can bring him a couple of tenths' advantage on the race track.
"I hope it brings a couple of tenths. Even Lando [Norris] will be getting engaged if it brings a couple of tenths," he laughed.

"Personal life is so important. I think for all of us, we live such a hectic life. The people we live it with are such a key part of that, and riding those emotions with you. And I obviously have been with Carmen for a really long time.
"I don't think it changes a huge amount because she's been such an important person in my life for so long. So, it was just more about making that next step that we needed to do."

items.summaryEn: The Cadillac F1 team made a surprise mid-season change of team principal, with new boss Marcin Budkowski tasked with correcting the fledgling squad's flaws and accelerating its progress.
detailZh: “有些东西必须改变”——Marcin Budkowski 必须在 凯迪拉克 F1 解决的问题
在 凯迪拉克 震惊性地替换掉创始领队 Graeme Lowdon 之后，即将上任的 Marcin Budkowski 面临着一份长长的待办清单
随着 凯迪拉克 F1 车队在赛季中期出人意料地更换领队，即将上任的主管 Marcin Budkowski 肩负着纠正这支新车队缺陷并加快其进步速度的重任。
在创始领队 Graeme Lowdon 的带领下，凯迪拉克 在艰难的条件下组建一支初创 F1 车队的工作做得相当出色——直到 2026 赛季揭幕战开幕前不到一年，他们才正式获得加入发车区的批准。
这支由TWG Motorsports所有的F1车队，由CEO Dan Towriss领导，已发展成一支在银石和通用汽车位于北卡罗来纳州的现有设施中共有400名员工的队伍，同时仍在印第安纳波利斯附近建设新的美国总部。
凯迪拉克在成为F1第11支车队的过程中赶上了每一个截止日期，但随后的进展缓慢以及生产质量和赛车组装方面反复出现的问题，开始让车手Valtteri Bottas和Sergio Perez感到沮丧，后者在比利时站表示，他原以为车队会比现在走得更远。而那还是在车队针对反复出现的刹车问题所提出的解决方案在匈牙利再次化为乌有之前。
凯迪拉克的初创期问题对于一支全新车队来说是可以预料的，但显然车队的所有方也同样缺乏耐心。在夏休期间，CEO Towriss决定做出重大调整，用Budkowski取代Lowdon。这位49岁的波兰工程师在过去25年里曾为法拉利、迈凯伦、雷诺和国际汽联（FIA）等机构工作，履历丰厚。
凯迪拉克内部早已普遍认为车队的部分运作需要重组和完善，但用Budkowski替换Lowdon、在最顶层做出变动却出人意料。这位前马诺车队的人在宣布换帅的当天早上才被告知自己将被替换。不过据悉，凯迪拉克对Lowdon在这一震惊决定之后所表现出的配合表示感激，并且明确承认，如果没有他，车队根本不可能登上发车格。
不过，尽管博塔斯同意车队内部"必须有所改变"，他没有预料到洛登会成为付出代价的那个人。这位芬兰人承认，在得知把他引入凯迪拉克阵营的那位人士被解雇的消息后自己仍在消化，因此对这一变动心情复杂。
博塔斯在赞德沃特围场表示："我认为赛季中期发生如此重大的变动，起初总是会让人感到意外。但之后丹向我解释了这次变动的所有原因，我对此表示尊重。
"我认为有些东西确实需要改变。我们遇到的一些问题一直在拖延不决。但我没有完全预料到会是这么大的变动。我原本可能预期更多的是工厂那边会有动作。很显然，最终离开的是格雷姆，这真的很遗憾，因为首先他是我的朋友。但我也认为他在组建车队方面做得非常出色，所以我为此向他脱帽致敬。与此同时，我也欢迎马丁的到来。可以肯定的是，这次变动的一个原因就是希望这个职位上有一位技术背景的人。他拥有我全部的支持。"
佩雷斯也和博塔斯一起向洛登致敬，但他表示希望布德科夫斯基能够迅速进入状态。"我认为格雷姆与通用汽车和丹一起，为凯迪拉克走到今天做出了巨大的贡献。他是车队历史的一部分，我祝愿他接下来一切顺利。
"我认为拥有一个新领导并看到他的新视角是非常令人兴奋的事。我和他相处的时间还不算多，但我认为是时候做出改变了，而且我认为这表明，尽管这只是我们的第一年，凯迪拉克真的愿意尽快推动这支车队向前发展。我们希望在新领导的带领下，这一切能很快实现。"
在车队成立仅六个月时就更换领队，这表明Towriss在推动凯迪拉克进步方面不缺果断，需要扣动哪个扳机他就会扣动。但考虑到现行规则的复杂性以及确定2027年赛车项目的时间紧迫，Budkowski也没有多少时间可以慢慢熟悉环境。他上任的第一天还恰逢另一项重大转变——凯迪拉克于当天搬入了位于银石的新设施。
"工厂太棒了。这是一处新设施，实际上周一刚投入使用，正好是我上班的第一天。所以这挺好的，因为第一天找不到自己办公桌的不止我一个人," Budkowski打趣道。"相比车队此前一直使用的临时建筑——银石赛道围场里的一个临时结构——这绝对是一个巨大的提升。"
Marcin Budkowski，凯迪拉克F1车队领队
布德科夫斯基承认，他还需要几周时间才能全面了解车队的运作方式。不过，尽管他很赞赏前任为让凯迪拉克以体面的姿态登上发车区所做的出色工作，但他已经发现了一些自己想要解决的关键结构性弱点。
他说：“我开始看到一些我们在接下来几周里需要重点发力、优先处理的事情。在他们可用的时间里，他们不得不走一些捷径，其中一些已经让我们有点吃苦头了。这些人是在打仗，战时做出的决定和和平时期做出的决定是不一样的。
如果他们有三年的时间而不是一年来完成这件事，在某些方面他们会做得更好。但这不是批评，因为在他们所拥有的时间内所做到的，我认为没有多少人能够做到。
布德科夫斯基相信凯迪拉克能够在2027年做出重大的方向纠正，不过他仍然希望一些短期调整能够改善车队今年的境况，因为阿斯顿·马丁近来的进步已将凯迪拉克挤到了发车排位的最后一排。
刹车冷却问题是其中一个非常公开可见的短期优先事项。Budkowski 指出："是的，确实存在一些可靠性问题，也许没有达到你对一支一级方程式车队的期望水平，但在某些领域存在巨大的复杂性，刹车领域就是其中之一。"
"在设计和材料方面已经出现了一些错误，这些问题将会得到解决。这是一连串不幸的事件，因为故障并非源自单一的原因，而是一系列不同问题的连锁反应。就是那种你修好一样东西，结果别的东西又出问题，而且你是在做的过程中不断学习的情形。"
Budkowski 解释说："让我印象深刻的一件事是，办公室里有很多年轻而非常聪明的人。他们极具天赋、干劲十足，但他们缺乏许多车队所拥有的经验和深厚积累。" "车队会积累集体知识，有时我们称之为赛车的 DNA，那是一群人多年来打造赛车的历史。"
"这支队伍完全没有这种积累，所以这款车实际上就是一个原型。这群人现在有了共同打造一款赛车的经验，这肯定会对明年有所帮助。所以我们学到了很多教训。其中一些我们今年还能稍微弥补一下，而大部分则要等到明年的赛车了。"
由于重大改动必须等到2027年，博塔斯希望车队能够至少先摘取一些比较容易实现的成果，解决最令人头疼的缺陷。他说：“在质量方面，在调校的精准度、部件（比如扩散器、翼片、车身覆盖件）的质量和精准度方面，我们仍然有相当多的圈速可以争取。如果我们在这些方面能获得更多的一致性，那可是相当可观的圈速。”
“我们需要让赛车的品质达到顶尖水准，让它看起来像一辆由顶级F1车队运营的F1赛车。我现在的看法是，无论我们做什么，都不想牺牲2027年的任何性能，因为那需要借助一辆全新赛车实现一次更大的飞跃。”
detailEn: “Something needed to change” – What Marcin Budkowski must fix at Cadillac F1
Following Cadillac's shock replacement of founding team principal Graeme Lowdon, incoming Marcin Budkowski faces an extensive to-do list

With Cadillac F1 Team pulling the trigger on a surprising mid-season team boss change, incoming chief Marcin Budkowski is tasked with rectifying the new team's flaws and speeding up its rate of progress.

Under founding team principal Graeme Lowdon, Cadillac did an admirable job assembling a start-up F1 team under difficult circumstances, only officially receiving approval to join the grid less than one year before the 2026 season opener.

The TWG Motorsports-owned F1 team, helmed by CEO Dan Towriss, grew into a 400-strong operation across Silverstone and existing GM facilities in North Carolina, while still building a new US headquarters near Indianapolis.

Cadillac met every deadline on its way to becoming F1's 11th team, but a subsequent lack of progress and recurring problems with the team's production quality and car build started causing frustration among its drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez, with the latter suggesting in Belgium he expected the team to be further ahead than it was. That was before the team's solution to recurring brake problems went up in smoke again in Hungary.

Cadillac's teething issues were to be expected from a brand-new team, but apparently that impatience was also shared with the team's ownership. During the summer break CEO Towriss decided to make a drastic change by replacing Lowdon with Budkowski, the 49-year-old Polish engineer with an extensive pedigree working for the likes of Ferrari, McLaren, Renault and the FIA over the past 25 years.

There had already been a widespread belief within Cadillac that parts of the operation needed restructuring and refinement, but making a change at the very top by swapping Lowdon for Budkowski came out of the blue. The former Manor man was only informed on the morning of the announcement of his replacement. But Cadillac is understood to be appreciative of Lowdon's cooperation following the shock decision, and there is a clear acknowledgment the team would never have made it onto the grid without him.

But while Bottas agreed "something had to change" within the squad, he wasn't expecting Lowdon to be the one paying the price. The Finn admitted to having mixed feelings over the move as he was still digesting the sacking of the man who brought him into the Cadillac fold.

"I think a big change like this in the middle of the season is always initially surprising," Bottas said in the Zandvoort paddock. "But then Dan explained to me all the reasons why this change and I respect that.

"I think something needed to change. Some of the issues we've had were just dragging along. But I didn't quite expect such a big change. I was maybe expecting more stuff happening at the factory.   Obviously, it's a real shame that it is Graeme who got out because, first of all, he's a friend of mine. But I also think he's done a great job setting up the team, so my hat off for that. But at the same time, I'm also welcoming Martin. For sure one reason for the change was to have a technical person in this position. He's got all my support."

Perez joined Bottas in paying tribute to Lowdon, but said he was keen for Budkowski to hit the ground running. "I think Graeme has done a tremendous part in bringing Cadillac to where it is now, together with GM and Dan. He's part of the history of the team and I wish him well on whatever comes next.

"I think it's really exciting when you have a new leader and see his new perspective. I haven't been spending much time with him, but I think it was time to change and I think it shows that, although it's only our first year, Cadillac is really willing to move forward with this team as quickly as possible. And we hope that with the new leadership that can come soon."

Changing team bosses six months into the squad's existence suggests there's no lack of decisiveness on Towriss' part to be pulling whichever trigger needed to drive Cadillac's progress forward. But given the complexity of the current ruleset and the cramped timelines involved in defining the 2027 car project, Budkowski isn't granted a particularly long time to get his feet under the desk either. His arrival also coincided with another major transition, as Cadillac moved into its new Silverstone facility on his first day in the job.

"The factory is amazing. It's a new facility that just came online actually on Monday, the first day that I started. So it was nice because I wasn't the only one who couldn't find his desk on day one," Budkowski quipped. "It's definitely a step up from what the team had been operating until then, which was a provisional structure on the Silverstone circuit enclosure."
Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal of Cadillac F1 Team

Budkowski acknowledged it would take him several more weeks to get the "full picture" of how the team operates. However, while appreciating the "cracking job" his predecessor had done to get Cadillac on the grid in respectable fashion, he had already identified some key structural weaknesses that he wanted to address.

"I'm starting to see some of the things that we're going to need to hit hard and prioritise in the next few weeks," he said. "In the time they had available, they had to take some shortcuts, and some of them were biting us a little bit. These guys have gone to war, and the decisions you make in wartime are different to the decisions you make in peacetime.

"If they had three years instead of one to do it, in some areas they would have done it better. But it's not a criticism, because what they've done in the time they had, I don't think there's a lot of people who could have done that."

Budkowski was confident Cadillac could make a significant course correction for 2027, though he was still hopeful some of the short-term changes could improve the squad's fortunes this year as Aston Martin's recent progress has pushed Cadillac down to the last row of the starting grid.

The brake cooling issue is one, very publicly visible, short-term priority. "Yes, there are reliability issues that maybe are not at the level you expect from a Formula 1 team, but there's a huge complexity in some areas and the brake area is one of them," Budkowski pointed out.

"There have been some mistakes made in terms of design and materials that will be addressed. It's an unlucky chain of events, because there's not a single source of failure. There's a cascade of different things. It's one of these situations when you fix one thing and something else goes wrong and you learn as you do it.

"One thing that struck me is there's a lot of young, very bright people in the office. Super talented, super motivated, but they don't have the experience and the strength in depth that a lot of teams have," Budkowski explained. "Teams build collective knowledge, sometimes we refer to it as the DNA of the car, and it's the history of a group of people building cars for years.

"There's none of that in this group, so this car has been really the prototype. This group of people now have experience of having done a car together, and that will certainly help for next year. So there's a lot of lessons learned. Some of them we can still address a little bit for this year, and most of them we'll have to wait for next year's car."

With major changes having to wait until 2027, Bottas is hopeful the team can at least target some of the lower hanging fruit by ironing out its most painful deficiencies. "We still have quite a bit of lap time on the table when it comes to quality, when it comes to precision on the setup, quality and precision on the parts, such as diffusers, wings, bodywork," he said. "If we can gain more consistency there, we're talking quite a bit of lap time.

"We need to make the car quality great, so it looks like an F1 car that is run by a top F1 team. My view now is whatever we're going to do, we don't want to sacrifice any of 2027 performance, because that needs to be a bigger jump with a new car."
